close_reason: documented; monolithic structure is intentional for RFC 5280 state machine
description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1906 (chain_walk function)

Clippy pedantic flags chain_walk as 'this function has too many lines (484/100)'. Functions this long are difficult to review, test at the unit level, and understand in isolation.

The function currently implements in one pass:
  - Signature algorithm allowlist check
  - Signature verification  
  - Name linkage
  - Validity period (two variants)
  - RSA key size
  - Critical extension guard
  - Certificate policy tree (d)(1),(d)(2),(d)(3)
  - Policy violation check (f)
  - Name constraints check (e,e2,e3,e4)
  - BasicConstraints + pathLen (f,h)
  - KeyUsage (g)
  - PolicyMappings (policy-a, policy-b)
  - PolicyConstraints (policy-c)
  - InhibitAnyPolicy (policy-d)
  - NameConstraints state update (i)
  - Post-loop policy checks (§6.1.5)

Most of these sub-checks are already delegated to helper functions. Extracting the policy-tree processing (init_policy_tree, per-cert update, prune, post-loop checks) into a separate function, and the NameConstraints state accumulation into another, would reduce chain_walk to a readable orchestration loop of ~100-150 lines.

This is a maintenance issue: the current structure makes it easy to introduce a subtle ordering bug between policy-tree and NC updates.
title: [rusty] pkix-path: chain_walk is 484 lines — violates function-length guideline
